subject: Art and Design
framework: National Curriculum in England (2013, in force from 2014): Art and design programmes of study, key stages 1 to 3; Early Years Foundation Stage (Expressive Arts and Design) for Reception
statusNote: Verified from official text read in full: National Curriculum art and design programmes of study (gov.uk, key stages 1 to 3, re-read October 2026); EYFS Expressive Arts and Design and Fine Motor early learning goals (statutory framework from 1 September 2026); DfE GCSE art and design subject content (January 2015). The AQA page is cited only as an example of assessment objectives. Statutory statements are by key stage; the year-by-year allocation is a recommended sequence, not statutory. Units marked inSchoolLessons are in the school's lesson files (two per year); other units are recommended additions with no lesson plans yet. School-choice notes, not verification gaps: the Google Drive Art scheme was not read; the GCSE board for Year 10 is not yet chosen, so no board unit references are given; Islamic art units follow the school lessons, as the National Curriculum names no artists or traditions. Year 1 was rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack: one unit per half term, following Tarbiyyah Primary's Cornerstones projects (2026-27 order), White Rose maths and Little Wandle phonics. Years 2 to 9 were rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA curriculum packs (docs/curriculum-packs/y2.md to y9.md): one unit per half term, titled by half term so the portal planner places each one. November 2026 alignment with the school's own files: Years 7 to 9 follow the order and topics of the Tarbiyyah Secondary Art & Design Curriculum Intent (Year 7: elements of art, colour theory, still life, buildings and Hundertwasser, silhouette art, Post-Impressionism; Year 8: perspective, Islamic art, abstract art, the hand in clay, tie-dye, street art and typography; Year 9: natural forms, Fauvism, optical illusion, flower power, architecture, an abstract final composition). The Creative Arts 5-year scheme in the folder is another school's (Redstone Academy) example scheme: its still life, buildings, silhouette, optical illusion, abstract, architecture and flower topics match the intent; its portraits, human figure, wildlife, vehicles, duff lessons and outdoor trips are not adopted, nor is the intent's visiting-artist workshop.

purpose: Art, craft and design are among humanity's creative achievements and shape history and culture.
Teaching should build skill, experimentation and original work, with deeper critical thinking in older pupils.
Pupils should record ideas, master drawing, painting, sculpture and other techniques, and evaluate work using subject vocabulary.
Pupils should learn about notable artists, craft makers, designers and architects and how their fields developed.

toKS4: Key stage 3 prepares pupils for GCSE Art and Design, where the four assessment objectives are, in general terms: develop ideas through investigation informed by sources (AO1); refine work by experimenting with media and processes (AO2); record ideas and observations (AO3); present a personal, informed outcome (AO4). In the AQA GCSE example opened, each objective carries 25% across a portfolio (60%) and an externally set assignment (40%). Year 9 sketchbook, drawing, design and research units build those habits. The school's GCSE board and endorsement are not confirmed, so no unit references are given. The DfE GCSE subject content (January 2015, read in full) requires drawing to support development in every area of study, allows entirely digital or non-digital work, and lists seven titles: art, craft and design; fine art; graphic communication; textile design; three-dimensional design; photography; critical and contextual studies. Year 7 to 9 units on sketchbooks, drawing, painting, printmaking, sculpture, textiles, photography and digital work map to these titles.
